title: Constant sheaf on a site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal A$ a category of values in which sheafification exists (sets, abelian groups, rings). For an object $E$ of $\mathcal A$ the *constant sheaf* $\underline E$ on $\mathcal C$ is the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the constant presheaf $U\mapsto E$, all of whose restriction maps are the identity of $E$. For a commutative ring $A$ the constant sheaf of rings $\underline A$ is a sheaf of commutative rings; on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ it is written $A_Y$.

source.place: Stacks Project, Sites and Sheaves, Example sites-example-constant-sheaf (Tag 0H7J); Bhatt-Scholze, The pro-etale topology for schemes, Example 4.2.10, p. 30 (constant sheaf on X_proet; literature/bhatt-scholze-pro-etale-topology_arXiv-1309.1198.pdf)
